messages:
alex: FYI we saw a weird cold-start pattern with encrypted safetensors bundles today. small chat request (20 tokens) took ~1.9s to return, root cause looks like synchronous bundle decrypt + multiple tiny reads. thinking: split manifest + payload and do manifest-first scheduling to get a small useful model subset online quickly

nina: sounds promising. can you sketch what "manifest-first" actually contains? minimal fields?

alex: minimal manifest = bundle-id, version, per-shard id/byte-range, shard_role (kv|embed|base|quant_delta), enc_meta (kms_key_id, key_version), sig. small enough to decrypt fast and cache. payload stays in opaque encrypted blobs.

sam: operational constraints: KMS has cost and rate limits. we should avoid N KMS calls per host on burst. proposal: manifest decrypt calls are cheap and cached locally (LRU by bundle-id+keyv). but payload decrypts are gated by a host-wide semaphore to avoid KMS/throttling storms.

alex: exactly. also add per-request heuristic: if request touches only KV prefixes, only warm shards with role==kv. If request requires full context, raise min_ready_set to base+kv.

nina: how does this interact with quant deltas? could we let inference start on base weights and stream in int4 deltas asynchronously?

sam: yes but need deterministic correctness surface. runtime should support "graceful-precision-upgrade" where model runs on base precision until quant overlay applied. add signal `on_precision_upgrade` so tracing/eval can mark any regressions.

alex: security: do not trust unverified hints. manifest must be signed by trusted registry key. If signature missing, runtime treats shard_role as unknown and uses conservative ordering (base then kv). signed_manifest should carry hint_trust_level in header.

nina: failure modes: what if manifest says shard at object A but payload fetch returns 404 or checksum mismatch? fallback options: (1) try alternate replica, (2) re-download bundle-level payload from origin and re-verify, (3) fall back to a smaller model variant if policy permits. we should make this configurable via "resilience_policy" in manifest.

sam: implementation sketch: 1) sidecar decryptor that exposes unix socket with two RPCs: decrypt_manifest(bundle_ref) -> manifest_json, and stream_shard(bundle_ref, shard_id) -> io_handle. 2) loader registers callbacks: on_manifest(manifest), on_shard_ready(shard_id). 3) runtime calls get_minimum_set(manifest, request_profile) to decide readiness threshold.

alex: keep WeightSource API backwards-compatible: add optional flags in options map: manifest_first=true|false, min_ready_set=[roles], allow_precision_degrade=true. if absent, current blocking semantics unchanged.

nina: metrics to add: manifest_decrypt_ms, manifest_sig_verify_ms, shards_scheduled, concurrent_decrypts, time_to_minimum_ready_ms, time_to_quant_overlay_ms, kms_calls_per_min. also track p50/p95/p99 for manifest path specifically.

sam: Dedicated vs Private: default sidecar placement = per-host for latency. For Private deployments we can support a shared decryptor inside VPC to centralize KMS access and HSMs. doc should recommend per-host for typical Dedicated unless customer has strict KMS quota optimizations.

alex: trust model: signer registry + key rotation. manifest cache must include signer_key_version and expiry. provide API to invalidate manifest cache via webhook from KMS or registry on rotation/revocation. TTL also enforced (default 30m).

nina: attack surface: a malicious bundle could craft a manifest that prioritizes shards to cause hot-path IO pressure. enforce server-side admission: signed manifests from our registry only, and per-tenant rate limits on parallel decrypts. plus a scheduling cost model that bounds shards per-second warmed.

sam: backpressure & safety: host semaphore for concurrent decrypts + per-tenant token bucket for shard warmups. also track memory pressure: do not bring more shards into GPU memory than mem_budget allows; queue lower-priority shards.

alex: rollout plan: spike week -> implement sidecar proto + loader hooks. bench microbench: random prefix-lengths (1,4,16,64 tokens) and bundle layouts (many small shards vs few big shards). metrics to capture: cold latency, p95 KMS latency impact, disk seek overhead. we'll need a synthetic library for bundle shapes.

nina: docs: update loader contract doc and WeightSource sample code. add migration notes for partners who produce bundles - sign manifests and annotate shard_role.

oracle-bot: ticket INF-4290 created: "manifest-first staged hydration + sidecar decryptor" (owner: alex, reviewers: nina,sam). ETA: spike in sprint-28.

sam: agree to prototype. volunteers: alex + sam for sidecar and loader, nina for security/signature work. alex: i'll draft a short RFC with wire proto and scheduling rules today.

nina: one more: include an "opt-in mandatory" knob for customers to require signed manifests only, so we can enforce production policies for high-security tenants.

alex: good. thanks all :rocket:
